subject: Clarify: backup garbage collection, retention windows and deletion propagation

Subject: Backup deletion question for Acme Payments (data residency)

Hi Jonas,

Quick question as we prep for our security review: we need to understand how Redwood handles user-initiated data deletion when that data is also present in backups and DR snapshots. Specifically:

- If a customer (or end-user) submits a deletion request for a record, how and when does that deletion propagate to backups and cross-region replicas?
- Are backups region-scoped (i.e., do backups for our US region remain in the US), and can we opt-out of cross-region replication?
- Can you confirm retention default windows and whether there is an expedited purge option for regulated data?

We have a SOC2 control that requires demonstrable removal or an accelerated purge path for PII when legally requested. Any short doc or example timeline would be great.

Thanks,
Sara Liao
Security & Compliance, Acme Payments

Sara — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers first, then I'm looping in Priyom (security) and Lauren (product) for the operational and offer-side details.

High level:
- Backups are by default retained 90 days (hosted) and are region-scoped. Cross-region replication is off by default for hosted customers; it can be enabled for DR at the account level.
- Standard snapshots are immutable for the retention window — a primary delete does not immediately remove data from existing backup snapshots. Instead, deletion is honored on the primary and the data becomes unreachable once backups expire or are garbage-collected according to the retention policy.
- For regulated customers we provide two options: (1) reduce retention window to a configured shorter period; (2) expedited purge (available for Dedicated and Private) where we coordinate a purge workflow — this can include KMS key rotation/deletion and manual GC.

Next steps: Priyom — can you confirm the exact technical steps and any security attestation we provide (SOC2 excerpt, purge SLA)? Lauren — I can sketch an MAA and pricing for the expedited purge add-on.

Best,

Hi Sara / team — adding technical detail and constraints so you have something to present to your auditors.

Technical behavior (hosted):
- Region scoping: backups and snapshots are stored in the same cloud region by default (your tenant's region). Cross-region replication is opt-in; if you opt in, replicas are encrypted and have identical retention policy but are stored in the configured replica region.
- Retention & GC: default 90-day retention; snapshots are incremental (block-level) with immutable manifests. Garbage collection runs on a rolling schedule (daily for active accounts), which physically reclaims space once the retention window expires. Because of the immutable manifest model, deletion from primary does not alter historical snapshots until GC removes the blocks. In practice, that means deletion propagation to physical removal can lag by up to the retention window plus the GC cycle.
- Expedited purge options: for Dedicated/Private customers we offer a documented purge pathway: (a) identify objects/keys to purge, (b) create a purge job, (c) rotate/revoke KMS keys (optional, for cryptographic destruction), (d) run an immediate GC pass on affected storage nodes, and (e) produce an audit log and certificate of purge. This process is not available for standard hosted accounts unless under a contract amendment.

Notes & caveats:
- For hosted accounts we can support reduced retention windows (e.g., 30/14/7 days) configurable at account level, which materially reduces the exposure period without needing an expedited purge.
- Legal hold / e-discovery overrides retention; if you place a hold we pause GC for those objects.
- We can provide a SOC2 excerpt that maps controls to backup/retention behavior — attaching the snippet.

Attachment: SOC2-backup-excerpt.pdf
Link: https://redwood-internal.kb/backups/gc-behavior

Happy to jump on a short call to run through a proof plan.

1) Scope decision (week 0): confirm region, choose retention profile (30 / 90 / custom), decide on cross-region replication.
2) Pilot (week 1–2): enable account-level shorter retention or provision Dedicated pilot for expedited purge. Run deletion test vector and produce audit trail.
3) Production rollout (week 3–4): apply configuration, update runbooks, provide final attestation.

Offer details:
- Hosted: configurable retention down to 7 days (no immediate physical purge). 90-day default.
- Dedicated/Private add-on: expedited purge service (+ one-off engineering effort) and certificate of destruction. Pricing TBD; I attached a draft MAA and scope worksheet.
